transcript: Last night my friend PJ and I went to see the Thanksgiving play on Broadway. This play was so funny. It's a satirical depiction of 4 people trying to devise culturally sensitive Thanksgiving play for an elementary school. The characters all come in with different levels of understanding of what this would necessitate in terms of including Native American voices in the piece, but regardless, all of them show their blind spots in the realm of cultural competence in theater making and in general. I laughed, I cringed, I gasped, and I loved how the play boldly shows how ignorance, even under actions with good intentions, can cause a wide array of outcomes ranging from humor all the way to violence. I also think this play is quite relevant right now with there being so much contentious debate about rewriting history and educational settings and removing some histories altogether. With that, another playbook for my collection.
